messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: model-inference-service increased 5xx rate and CUDA/NCCL errors detected from 2024-07-30T22:12Z. paging maya (oncall) / runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nccl-collective-failure

maya (oncall): joining, thanks. getting the incident page. can someone paste a quick summary of customer impact?

sam (sre): seeing a cluster-wide spike in 'NCCL WARN' and 'unhandled cuda error' in runtime logs. Affected pool: inference-gpu-prod, ~12 pods across 4 nodes flapping. Errors look like communicator timeouts / unreachable peers.

chris (ml-infra): logs from one replica:
```
[2024-07-30 22:10:12] ERROR runtime: NCCL WARN Call to connect returned error Unreachable; peer 2
[2024-07-30 22:10:13] ERROR runtime: ncclCommEnqueue failed: Unhandled system error
[2024-07-30 22:10:13] ERROR runtime: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure (kernel)
[2024-07-30 22:10:13] ERROR runtime: TensorParallelGroup 0 hang detected, aborting communicator
```

leo (runtime): Also seeing GPU resets on nodes. nvidia-smi loop shows repeated GPU reinitialization and high RX/TX on IB. Suspect NCCL collective stuck then watchdog kills job.

frank (support): Customer impact: LogixHealth and BrightCart report degraded inference latencies / 5xx. Support tickets #8243 #8244 opened. Defaulting to P1 since production traffic is affected.

maya (oncall): TL;DR for handoff: NCCL multi-GPU collectives are failing across several nodes, causing containers to crash or hang. We paged SRE and ml-infra. Current mitigation attempts?

sam (sre): Mitigations in progress:
- cordon/evict pods on two most-affected nodes (node-34, node-35)
- restart runtime containers on those nodes
- route small fraction of traffic to fallback single-GPU variant (model-small-1gpu) via routing rule to reduce multicast collectives

chris (ml-infra): Quick troubleshooting steps we've tried: set NCCL_DEBUG=WARN, enabled NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 on one service, set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=^docker, increased verbosity. Also tested disabling IB by NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 on one node to isolate whether RDMA is the issue. With IB disabled, the node reconnects and jobs proceed for a while but throughput degrades.

leo (runtime): Command snippets we ran:
```bash
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/model-inference-service
ssh node-34 sudo systemctl restart docker
# inspect dmesg for GPU reset
dmesg | grep -i nvrm
# env overrides for test pod
export NCCL_DEBUG=WARN NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0
```

chris (ml-infra): Observed additional log lines when IB disabled:
```
NCCL INFO Transport: sockets (fallback)
NCCL INFO : using 1/1 channels
NCCL WARN > communicator timeout after 120000ms
```
Which suggests timeouts remain under some traffic patterns. We increased NCCL_TIMEOUT from default 30s to 120s in tests — helped reduce immediate failures but doesn't fix root cause.

maya (oncall): Good. For immediate mitigation let's: 1) keep routing 30% traffic to single-GPU fallback, 2) drain the two nodes that showed repeated GPU resets and repro them in isolation, 3) enable temporary auto-retry/backoff in the runtime so a bad communicator doesn't kill the request path.

sam (sre): Agreed. I'm creating a short-lived circuit-breaker in the edge router to reduce concurrency per connection and enable faster fallbacks. Also ramping down batch sizes to reduce memory pressure.

frank (support): Notifying affected customers: LogixHealth and BrightCart have been informed of partial outage, ETA for mitigation ~45m. I'll update tickets with current mitigations and link to incident page.

chris (ml-infra): Additional debugging commands for SRE to capture before draining nodes:
```bash
# capture nccl params and status
ps aux | grep nccl
nccl-tests --gtest_filter=All -w 10 --nthreads 4  # reproduce collectives under stress (scheduled)
# collect output from syslog/dmesg and nvtop
journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 > /tmp/kubelet.log
dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg_gpus.log
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,POWER,UTIL -l 1 > /tmp/nvidia_snap.log &
```

leo (runtime): Note: we also found a stacktrace in one runtime core dump referencing ncclNetProxy and 'send timeout'. Possible driver-level mismatch on node-35 (driver 515.x vs 520.x). I'm asking infra to verify driver versions across nodes.

maya (oncall): Action items captured:
- sam: implement router circuit-breaker and ramp fallback traffic (in progress)
- leo: drain node-34 / node-35, capture logs, repro with nccl-tests, collect core dumps (in progress)
- chris: prepare a patched runtime with NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and increased NCCL_TIMEOUT for canary (staging)
- frank: continue customer comms and update tickets
- all: gather pack of logs (dmesg, kubelet, nv-smi, runtime logs) and attach to incident page

sam (sre): Router change applied: 30% -> single-GPU fallback, concurrency cap lowered by 40%. Early signals: 5xxs down 65% in last 5m.

chris (ml-infra): We pushed a canary with env overrides to staging and one production replica with NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1, NCCL_TIMEOUT=180000. Canary looks stable for ~10m. We'll hold for 15m before wider rollout.

frank (support): Updated customers: logged update that mitigations are rolling out, reduced errors, ETA 30–60m for full stabilization. Both customers acknowledged.

leo (runtime): Found driver mismatch: node-35 has older NVIDIA driver (515.65) vs cluster standard 520.61.1. I'm isolating node-35 and scheduling driver upgrade; suspect driver/IB firmware mismatch triggered NCCL disconnects.

maya (oncall): Handoff note for next oncall (if I need to sign out):
- Incident: NCCL/multi-GPU collective failures causing container crashes and hangs across inference pool.
- Status: circuit-breaker + 30% fallback active, two nodes drained (node-34 repro in progress, node-35 isolated for driver upgrade). Canary with async error handling and extended NCCL_TIMEOUT looks promising.
- Impacted customers: LogixHealth, BrightCart (partial P1).
- Next steps: finish node driver upgrades, roll canary to remaining replicas, collect postmortem artifacts (nccl logs, core dumps, nv-smi), plan a low-risk upgrade of NCCL/driver stack and run extended stress tests.

chris (ml-infra): I'll open a follow-up ticket to schedule a rolling driver/NCCL upgrade with compatibility tests and add a deterministic repro harness in CI.

maya (oncall): Thanks everyone. I'll unassign the page when sam confirms router is stable and chris confirms canary hold is good. Leaving detailed notes on the incident page. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident page updated: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-20240730-09 (updated by maya)
